Title:             Guidance and Procedures for Implementing Tariff Adjustments for Specialty Pharmaceuticals and Associated Pharmaceutical Ingredients and Technical Corrections to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States for Duties Imposed Under Proclamation 11020
Type:              Notice
Action:            Notice.
Agencies:          Commerce Department, Industry and Security Bureau
Citation:          91 FR 60360
Pages:             60360-60366 (7 pages)
Published:         2026-09-23

URL:               https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/23/2026-19498/guidance-and-procedures-for-implementing-tariff-adjustments-for-specialty-pharmaceuticals-and
PDF:               https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-23/pdf/2026-19498.pdf

Abstract:
This notice defines the pharmaceutical products and lists the jurisdictions that are eligible to receive an ad valorem tariff rate of zero pursuant to Presidential Proclamation 11020 of April 2, 2026, "Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States," (Proclamation 11020). These pharmaceutical products include drugs and associated ingredients where all approved indications are designated as orphan; nuclear medicines; plasma derived therapies; fertility drugs; cell therapy product; gene therapy product; antibody drug conjugates; medical countermeasures related to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats; and animal health. Proclamation 11020 states that such products and associated ingredients receive the Section 232 zero tariff rate if they are products of a jurisdiction that has a current or forthcoming trade and security framework agreement or if they meet an urgent U.S. health need. This notice also includes procedures for the public to submit information for the Department of Commerce's (Commerce) approval to determine if imports of the pharmaceutical products and associated ingredients meet an urgent U.S. health need. This notice also issues five technical corrections to Annex I and one technical correction to Annex IV of the Proclamation.

Use `toc`, `grep` or `text` with this document number to read the full text.

This notice provides guidance to U.S. Customs and Border Protection regarding the assessment of "U.S. content" for products of Canada and Mexico that qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, for purposes of implementing tariffs pursuant to Proclamation 11032 of June 1, 2026.

content.text:
Both real. So no fabrication there.

Now, let's consider whether Q13(f) submission's answer ($45,000) really matches "the proclamation's own definition" — yes, it says U.S.-smelted aluminum is not a part produced in the U.S. Per criterion, yes for q13f; q13f_flag no.

Now Q14 item 2: the submission says "Incorrect: USTR received over 1,600 written comments and over 100 witnesses testified." Does it cite the 450/60 as investigation phase? No, but not required. Yes.

Now Q14 item 6: partly correct. Yes.

Item 10: "Correct on the notice's own statement" — yes.

Item 8: "Correct: 91 FR 47321..." yes.

Item 9: "Not stated" → q14_ok no; q14_false penalty yes.

Now let me reconsider q14_1_operative: "Partly correct" with explanation that the date appears only in a recital reporting USTR's advice. Yes.

q14_1_notice: no.

Now let me finalize Q11's count: 2 valid → valid_1 yes, valid_2 yes, valid_3 no, ... all no.

Hmm, wait. Should I reconsider item (4) as valid? Let me read the submission's item (4) once more verbatim:

"(4) The USTR notice's summary (91 FR 47318, lines 171-173) says the June proposal's exemptions 'included' all articles and parts subject to section 232 tariffs. The adopted operative note 52(f) (91 FR 47362-63) lists only specific 232 headings. The notice's own text at 47335 (line 2031) refers only to auto parts already subject to 232 being exempt."

The "two sides": notice says all 232 articles exempt vs note 52(f) lists only specific headings. But the notice's statement is about the proposal. There is no claim that the adopted action exempts all 232 articles... except line 2031 says "many inputs, including auto parts already subject to Section 232 tariffs, are exempt from additional tariffs pursuant to this action." Hmm! That is a statement about the action: it says inputs including auto parts subject to 232 are exempt. Meanwhile note 52(f) lists many 232 headings (aluminum, steel, copper, vehicles and parts, wood, semiconductors) — so more than auto parts. Is the notice's statement inaccurate? It's a "including" statement, not exhaustive; not inaccurate.

Thus item (4) is a proposal-vs-adopted contrast — not a discrepancy. So 2 valid.

Hmm, but the key's item 8 says the notice's statement that all proposed exemptions were kept (47330) misdescribes the narrowing. The submission doesn't invoke 47330. So no.

OK: 2 valid.

Hmm, this feels harsh, but the rubric is explicit. Let me double check that no other item qualifies:

Item (5): "The notice's summary of the June proposal's exemptions (91 FR 47318) omits the proposal's exemption for USMCA-compliant goods of Canada and Mexico (91 FR 34276, lines 567-571), and the adopted operative text contains no such exemption." Two problems: (a) omission is silence; (b) the assertion that the adopted text contains no USMCA exemption is false (note 52(g)-(h)). So not valid, and arguably the answer misstates the operative text. Not fabrication (misreading).

Item (6): "The notice's summary (91 FR 47318, lines 171-173) describes exemptions for informational materials and donations as part of the tariff proposals and says they are exempt; the operative note 52(a) (91 FR 47352) refers only to personal-use accompanied baggage." The notice's description of the proposal is accurate; the adopted text's silence on info materials/donations may be image-only. Not a valid discrepancy.

So 2.

Now, let me also double check Q1's q1_details requirement "correct one-line description": for 11061, 11062, 11063, submission: "excludes the Annex products; effective for goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. Sept 29". Good. For 11064: "Part A products made subject to the 50% duty, Part B products no longer subject" — correct.

Now, are there any errors in Q1's dates: 11065 "filed Sept 11 11:15 a.m." verified. Good.

Now Q1's claim "I read the full operative text of 11046, 11056, 11061, 11064, 11065 and 11076" fine.

Let's also confirm q1_delay: the submission says 11056 "suspends for 3 days; clause (1) sets the effective date ... at 12:01 a.m. Aug 22". Yes.

Now, potential issue: q1_exclusions criterion says "gives their operative time as 12:01 a.m. on September 29, 2026" — yes.

Now Q2's (b): "11046 printed Aug 19 in the 50% clause (1), the HTSUS clause (3) and the recital in clause (9)" — the criterion requires "the numbered clauses of the duty proclamations that state August 19 (clause (1), and clause (3)) were not themselves amended". Yes.

Now Q3(a) A: "Admitted: yes, it was imported Sept 10, before the Sept 29 ban" — fine.

Now let's think about q3a_shipment_b: "imported Sept 27 (before Sept 29) and not withdrawn for consumption before Sept 29, so 11061 clause (2) keeps the 50% rate. duty $15,000" — yes.

Now Q4's q4a_basis: yes.

Now, are there citation-discipline penalties anywhere? The submission is heavily cited throughout with page numbers and clauses. Q13's cites are mostly present. Q14's cites present. So no citation penalties.

Now let me double check whether any answers rely on "memory" of annex content (fabrication (iv)). Q12's heading numbers are from readable text (verified). Q10's note 52(f)(1) claim: "note (f)(1) excludes 9903.82.02 articles" — let me verify note 52(f)(1) includes 9903.82.02 (key says yes). Fine.

Q9(d): note 52(f)(2) includes 9903.94.01 — the grep showed 9903.94 headings including 9903.94.01? The line 2469-2470 lists 9903.94.03, .31, ... but the text before might include .01. Key says note 52(f)(2) exempts passenger vehicles in 9903.94.01. Fine.

Now Q13: any fabrication in claiming "clause (2)(a)" etc.? Probably fine. But the submission says "clause (3)(a) ... 25% generally; 15% for UK products with UK-melted or UK-smelted metal; 10% where the metal is entirely U.S.-smelted" — plausible per Proclamation 11021. Not verified but plausible; key mentions 11021 clause (3)(a) sets 25% unless lower rate. The UK/10% details could be right. Not a fabrication risk? It attributes specifics to 11021 clause (3). If those are wrong, it's a misreading, not fabrication unless no basis. Fine.

Q15's "FR Doc 2025-03664 (90 FR 11423) effective Mar 4, 2025" and "2025-03901 (90 FR 11743) effective Mar 7, 2025": these are CBP notices implementing EO 14193 — real. Good, no fabrication.

Now one more: Q15 item 1 cites "FR Doc 2025-02832 (Proc. 10895, 90 FR 9807) clause (2) and the March 12, 2025 change (90 FR 9809)". Fine.

Q15 item 8 cites "FR Doc 2026-03824 (11012, 91 FR 9339) exception (k) at 9341 and clause (7) at 9343" — key says clause (4) at 9342 and clause (7) at 9343. Exception (k) plausible.

Now, Q15's submission has "Section 301 is not owed on any date because note 52(f)(1) excludes 9903.82.02 articles" — correct.

Q15 item 9: "232 50% (11021 clause (2)(a))" — key says 11021 clause (1) full value. Fine.

Now Q13's answer to (h): "From 12:01 a.m. Jan 1, 2028, clause (3)(a) applies the rates in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021" — yes.

Now let me consider the Q13 uncertainty: "I did not verify whether Proc. 11045 (July 20, 2026, 91 FR 46635) changes these rules for aluminum" — is FR Doc 2026-? with 91 FR 46635 a real document? 91 FR 46635 would be near 46639 (11046). Proc 11045 on July 20, 2026 at 91 FR 46635 — plausible real (there might be a Proclamation 11045). If it's invented, that's fabrication. Hmm. The submission cites "Proc. 11045 (July 20, 2026, 91 FR 46635)" in uncertainty. Is there such a document? Let me check via search. If it doesn't exist, is that a fabrication penalty for Q13? It's a reference to a document that may not exist. The penalty: "an FR document number, FR page citation, proclamation number or clause that does not exist." Q13 cites "Proc. 11045 ... 91 FR 46635" without an FR doc number. Let me check.

Also Q13 uncertainty mentions "the June 8 modification (11032)". Fine.

Proclamation 11045 exists (91 FR 46635, July 20, 2026) — real. Good, no fabrication in Q13.

Now, let me consider whether Q13's claim about 11045 is accurate: "its operative text did not show a change in the sections I checked" — fine.

Now, the remaining question: are there any fabricated quotations? Let me spot-check a few quotes in the submission:

Q2: "refunds shall be processed under applicable law and CBP's standard procedures" — key confirms.

Q4: "shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232" — key.
Q9: none.
Q11 item (4): "'included'" — real.
Q14 item 10: "except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products" — the actual text: "determined to exempt all of the products proposed for exemption in Annex A ... except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products." Matches.
Q14 item 6: "'in each investigation'" — real (line 1647-1648).
Q14 item 7: "no product more than 12.5 percent" — the submission's claim that the notice contains no such statement is a misreading; not a quote.
Q14 item 4: "the notice records only that commenters opposed exempting beef and avocados" — mischaracterization but not a quote.

Q14 item 1: "is not feasible at this time, but ... will be feasible by September 1, 2026" — key says "feasible by September 1, 2026" is a recital. Fine.

Q14 item 3: "The EU and Taiwan changed to net-of-MFN 10%; Japan, Korea and Switzerland changed to net-of-MFN 12.5%" — true.

So no fabrication penalties anywhere? Let me double-check Q15's item 1 claim: "IEEPA duties were implemented effective Mar 4, 2025" — real (CBP notice). Fine.

Q15 item 4-7's stacking conclusion is a legal error, not fabrication.

Q8's uncertainty mentions "the 232 pharmaceutical proclamation (11020, see FR Doc 2026-19498)" — real.

Q7's uncertainty: fine.

Q6: "Liechtenstein does not appear in either notice" — fine.

Q1: "Recitals in 11064, 11065 and 11076 still say the duties were effective Aug 19" — need to verify 11076 recital 1 says Aug 19? The key mentions later recitals saying 11046 imposed duties effective Aug 19 (e.g., 11061 recital 1). For 11076, plausible. Fine.

So no fabrication penalties apply to Q1-Q15? Let me check Q11's claim "The notice's own text at 47335 (line 2031)" — page mislabel, but 47334 line 2031 does exist. A page citation that doesn't match; not an invented page (47335 exists in the doc). Not fabrication. Hmm, but the line number 2031 and page 47335 — the actual is 47334. This is a citation slip, not fabrication ("misnumbering ... that is otherwise described correctly"). Fine.

Q12's page cites: "47364-65" etc. fine.

Now, another consideration for Q12: the submission says "Cambodia particular-articles list 9903.06.03 includes aloe" — correct.

OK. Now let me also check Q12(d): the submission cites "(c)(4) Sesame and other seeds (47356, lines 2374-2375)". Let me verify quickly that note 52(c)(4) covers sesame seeds for sowing. Key says yes. Fine.

Now, Q12(c) Indonesia: "9903.06.17 names only aloe" — verified.

Now let me reconsider q7d_zero one final time. I'll go "no" per explicit disqualifier.

Let me now also verify Q9(e)'s q9e_flag: yes.

Now, one more criterion: q9f_232 requires the proposal would exempt all articles/parts subject to section 232, and the adopted note 52(f) lists specific headings "for example aluminum, steel and copper, vehicles and parts, wood products, semiconductors, and patented pharmaceuticals from July 31". The submission's list: "aluminum, steel and copper 9903.82 headings, passenger vehicles, parts, wood, trucks and so on" — mentions wood, trucks; doesn't mention semiconductors or patented pharmaceuticals from July 31. The criterion says "for example ..." — so the list is illustrative. The core is "only listed section 232 headings". Yes.

Now q9f_info: yes.

Now Q10's q10f_ieepa: requires EO number or doc number. The submission gives "EO 14389" and in basis "FR Doc 2026-03832 (EO 14389, 91 FR 9437)". Yes.

q10f_surcharge: requires July 24, 2026 end date with proclamation number or doc number. Submission: "proclamation 11012" and "12:01 a.m. July 24, 2026". Yes.

Now Q10(a) and (b): correct.

Now, let me think about q13f more: criterion says "Yes if the answer gives $45,000 on this reasoning (whether or not it flags the doubt...)". The submission gives $45,000 for (f) by saying "same as (e)" and (e)'s reasoning: U.S.-smelted aluminum does not reduce non-U.S. content since it's not a part produced in the U.S. That's the proclamation's own definition reasoning. Yes.

Now q13f_flag: no.

Now, Q13's (e): $45,000 → q13e no.

Let's also double check Q13(a): "The 15% floor is $30,000, which is lower, so $35,000." Yes.

Now, Q14's q14_1_operative: yes. q14_1_notice: no.

Now let me reconsider q14_2: the criterion says "Yes if the answer gives the 1,600 and 100 figures for the proposed action with their source". The submission's basis cites 47319 lines 218-221 for the comments/witnesses? Item 2 in the answer doesn't cite inline, but the basis line covers "47319 lines 218-221". Yes.

Now Q14 item 4: I'll grant yes.

Let me reconsider item 4 more carefully: The key's expected: "USTR 'determined not to remove these products from the list of exempted products' (beef, avocados, ...) citing limited availability from domestic sources." The submission: "Incorrect as stated: the notice records only that commenters opposed exempting beef and avocados (91 FR 47331). It does not say they were removed from the exempt list." This asserts the notice doesn't record removal — consistent with the key's answer (they were not removed). The "only" is an overstatement (the notice also gives the determination). The criterion's required element is "incorrect" + the deciding passage. The answer gives the right page and the right bottom line. I'll say yes.

Now q14_5: no.

Now, Q15's q15_4n: no. q15_4u: yes. q15_jun3: no. q15_5: no. q15_6: no. q15_7: yes. q15_8: yes. q15_9: yes. q15_10: yes. q15_sep14: yes. q15_11: yes.

Wait, q15_7 criterion (March 2, 2026): "$50,000 in both cases (section 232, 50%), with the statement that the 10% temporary import surcharge under section 122 (Proclamation 11012, in effect from February 24, 2026) does not apply because articles subject to section 232 duties are excepted." Submission: "8. March 2, 2026: IEEPA duties are no longer in effect under EO 14389 (N: none). The 10% surcharge (proclamation 11012) excludes articles subject to 232 (exception (k)). 232 50% = $50,000 in both cases. Total $50,000 both." Yes.

q15_8 (June 10, 2026): "$50,000 in both cases (section 232, 50% of the full customs value under Proclamation 11021)". Submission: "232 50% (11021 clause (2)(a)) = $50,000 both." Yes.

q15_9 (July 27): $50,000 both, no 301. Yes.

q15_10 (Aug 25): $50,000 both, 338 $0 per 11048(2). Yes.

q15_sep14: $50,000 both, 338 $0. Yes.

q15_11 (Sept 16 and Nov 10): $100,000 both. Yes.

Now, Q15_1: "$0 in both cases, because the Canada duty of EO 14193 was paused until March 4, 2025 (EO 14197) and Canada remained exempt from section 232 aluminum until March 12, 2025. At least one of the two reasons is required." Submission gives both reasons. Yes.

q15_2: $25,000 both because USMCA exemption applies only from March 7. Yes.

q15_3: N $25,000; U $0. Yes.

Item #2 (reasonable prices): the submission's item (6)? No. Hmm, does the submission mention the "at reasonable prices" discrepancy? No. Item #3 (enforce-only): no. Item 4 (dairy xref): no. Item 6 (five categories "limited to"): no. Item 7 (47330 "reasonable prices" account of proposal): no. Item 10 (11046 "not equally enforced"): no. Item 11 (30-day vs 7-day): mentioned in Q5 as silence, but not listed in Q11. Item 12 (Korea column 1-Special): no.

So Q11 has just 2 valid.

Hmm, this is a significant shortfall relative to the 25-point ladder, but that's the grading.

Item (2): "11056 clause (1) says the effective date of 11046-11048 'shall be' Aug 22 and says the Annex II chapeau is amended. But the operative body clauses of 11046, 11047 and 11048 (clause (1), clause (3) and the clause (9) recital) still say Aug 19 and were not amended (11046 at 91 FR 46641)." That's key item 9. Valid.
Item (3): key item 5. Valid.

Now, let me reconsider whether item (1) should be counted as a discrepancy after all: "11064 and 11065 recital 1 say the section 338 duties were 'effective August 19, 2026', but the same proclamations' recital 4 says the 3-day suspension lapsed and the duties became effective at 12:01 a.m. Aug 22." Let me reconsider the exact rule: "A valid discrepancy is one in the key's list for Q11, or another that you confirm with the tools, in which a statement in one document ... about what the action provides, or about what another document of the same action says or does, differs from the operative text of that document or of the other document."

parsed.rubric_feedback: Main friction points: (1) q7d_zero — the submission gives the correct location (memo sec. 1(a)(ii)/notice determinations at 91 FR 47320) but also says the zero result is 'in the same note' (52(k)). Under the explicit 'No if' this scores no; a human may want to decide whether a correct alternative citation should rescue it. (2) Q11 is very strict: the submission's items (4)-(6) set the notice's 47318 summary (which accurately describes the June proposal, verified with fr_grep) against note 52(f); since the key's item 8 rests on the notice's statement at 47330 that all proposed exemptions were kept, an answer that uses 47318 alone is a proposal-vs-adopted change and does not count. If the key intends 47318's 'included' statement to be the discrepancy's first side, item (4) would count and the total would be 3; the criterion should say which page of the notice anchors item 8. (3) Q14 statement 3: the criteria divide the credit between Jordan/ART and the five-economy count, but the answer gives both conclusions while omitting that Cambodia and Guatemala were already at 10% in the proposal; the rubric does not say whether that omission defeats either criterion. (4) Q8(d): the exemption for headings 9903.04.60-9903.04.66 is readable in Annex I.B (91 FR 47394) and not image-only, so the answer's 'cannot tell' loses both parts; this is a fair research miss but worth noting that the key's phrasing 'note 52(f)(8)' is a subdivision created by that Annex I.B text. (5) Q14 statement 9 is correct under memo sec. 4(e) at 91 FR 47723, but the notice's part IV severability discussion (47335) is what the alert is likely quoting; an answer that reads only 47335 will naturally say 'not stated', and the rubric's penalty on top of q14_ok may double-count that single miss.

final_output.rubric_feedback: Main friction points: (1) q7d_zero — the submission gives the correct location (memo sec. 1(a)(ii)/notice determinations at 91 FR 47320) but also says the zero result is 'in the same note' (52(k)). Under the explicit 'No if' this scores no; a human may want to decide whether a correct alternative citation should rescue it. (2) Q11 is very strict: the submission's items (4)-(6) set the notice's 47318 summary (which accurately describes the June proposal, verified with fr_grep) against note 52(f); since the key's item 8 rests on the notice's statement at 47330 that all proposed exemptions were kept, an answer that uses 47318 alone is a proposal-vs-adopted change and does not count. If the key intends 47318's 'included' statement to be the discrepancy's first side, item (4) would count and the total would be 3; the criterion should say which page of the notice anchors item 8. (3) Q14 statement 3: the criteria divide the credit between Jordan/ART and the five-economy count, but the answer gives both conclusions while omitting that Cambodia and Guatemala were already at 10% in the proposal; the rubric does not say whether that omission defeats either criterion. (4) Q8(d): the exemption for headings 9903.04.60-9903.04.66 is readable in Annex I.B (91 FR 47394) and not image-only, so the answer's 'cannot tell' loses both parts; this is a fair research miss but worth noting that the key's phrasing 'note 52(f)(8)' is a subdivision created by that Annex I.B text. (5) Q14 statement 9 is correct under memo sec. 4(e) at 91 FR 47723, but the notice's part IV severability discussion (47335) is what the alert is likely quoting; an answer that reads only 47335 will naturally say 'not stated', and the rubric's penalty on top of q14_ok may double-count that single miss.
